name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,241

clue.text: Book everything for party

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
everything is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone reserves the whole lot of something for a party they are throwing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as a verb meaning reserve, but it is the noun, shortened to its usual one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social gathering with dancing, a grand kind of festive event.

clue.text: Good place to go for long run in New York?

definitions.text: Good place to go for long run in New York?

blocks.clueFragment: Good place to go for long run
blocks.note: surface reading: a wide street that would suit a jogger going a long distance
setter's reading: a long run is a show staying on stage for many months in the city's famous theatre district

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like advice for runners, but a 'long run' is theatre jargon for a hit show playing night after night. The street name also splits as a broad way, a wide road for running.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Manhattan avenue gives its name to the theatre district where successful productions enjoy lengthy runs.

clue.text: Northern city is ahead of all others, according to reports

indicators.note: reports are things heard rather than read, so the word must be taken by its sound

blocks.note: whoever is ahead of everyone else leads the field

explanation.surface: A boast that some northern city tops every ranking, at least as the press tells it.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, in the north of England; its name is said exactly like the verb form 'leads'.
explanation.definitionFit: This major Yorkshire city lies in northern England, so the geographical description identifies it fairly.

clue.text: Game ultimately attracts frantic, unruly crowd

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each following word is wanted

blocks.note: final letter
final letter
a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A match draws in a wild, disorderly crowd of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' covers two words, not one: both 'attracts' and 'frantic' give up their last letters. 'Frantic' looks like a description of the crowd but is only there for its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is a well-known board game where players build words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Make wooden box to be filled with earth

indicators.note: whatever is filled has something else placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a crate is a wooden packing box
E is the usual abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Instructions to build a wooden box and then shovel soil into it, like a planter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like the start of an instruction about the box, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To create something is to bring it into being, a direct synonym for producing or building.

clue.text: Particular guys involved in relevant meeting

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is wrapped up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a particular, as a noun, is a detail or point
guys are men
apt means pertinent or relevant

explanation.surface: Specific people taking part in a meeting that matters to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' reads as an adjective describing the guys, but it is the noun meaning a detail, as in 'in every particular'.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointment is an arranged meeting at a set time, such as one with a doctor or client.

clue.text: Bishop and priest almost always have faith

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
ever means always

explanation.surface: Clergy of every rank keep their religious faith nearly all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest, from the Book of Samuel. 'Almost' applies only to the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe is to hold religious conviction or trust in something, which is what having faith means.

clue.text: Has lamb and chicken, say, but without a starter

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so lacking one means the opening letter goes

blocks.note: lamb and chicken are examples of meats

explanation.surface: Someone's dinner order of lamb and chicken, skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' in the meal sense is the misdirection: here it is the first letter of the word. 'Say' signals that lamb and chicken are examples.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal is to consume it, so 'has' can mean dines on or consumes food.

clue.text: Late deliveries initially didn’t unsettle employees

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the following words count

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Parcels arriving late, but at least the staff weren't upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries suggests post; in cricket, the bat-and-ball game, a bowler's set of six deliveries is called an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed the time it was expected, so it is behind schedule.

clue.text: Huge warship a thunder god destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, its parts scattered, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A massive battleship sunk by a storm-wielding deity such as Thor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a mythological story, but the god is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The dreadnought was an early twentieth-century class of big-gun battleship, named after the British vessel HMS Dreadnought.

clue.text: Storyline probed by one introductory episode

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so one piece is inserted inside the other

blocks.note: a plot is a storyline
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A TV series' plot gets examined through its opening instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface sounds like television criticism, which is the right world, but 'one' is only the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is the trial first instalment of a television series, made to test whether it gets commissioned.

clue.text: Horribly westernised, sweet drink

indicators.note: something done horribly is botched and mangled, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a traditional sweet drink has been ruined by Western influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westernised' looks like a description of the drink but supplies exactly the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert wines are sugary wines served with or as the final course, such as Sauternes or port.

clue.text: System periodically supporting big charity

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
in a down answer a support sits underneath, so this part follows the other

blocks.note: large means big
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An occasional scheme of backing for a major charitable organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big charity' looks like one phrase, a major charity, but 'big' belongs to the wordplay and 'charity' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, which is the sense of charity as benevolent donation.

clue.text: Where you may find gaming machines are broken open by scoundrel

definitions.text: Where you may find gaming machines

indicators.note: breaking something open lets another thing in, so one piece is inserted inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Slot machines being smashed into by a crook after the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a mere verb in the sentence, but it is the outer piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a venue full of coin-operated video and slot games.

clue.text: Jointly start company with nothing in kitty

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
O looks like zero
a kitty is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: Launching a business together with an empty bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start company' looks like the definition, but 'company' is the first piece of wordplay and 'Jointly start' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-found an organisation is to establish it together with one or more partners.

clue.text: Greek goddess seen in Sparta, then Alexandria

indicators.note: what is seen in a phrase is visible inside it, running across the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A goddess's statue spotted on a tour of ancient cities, first Sparta and later Alexandria.
explanation.walkthrough: The place names suggest a classical trivia question, but the answer is just sitting in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Olympian deity of wisdom and warfare, patron of the city of Athens.

clue.text: An endless job for lead TV presenter

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: Fronting a TV programme as a never-ending grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' seems to describe the job's tedium, but it trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter of a news broadcast who links reports from other correspondents.

clue.text: Struggling Romeo finally falling short in casual relationship

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept
one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: final letter
to fall short of a target is to come in under it
a fling is a short casual affair

explanation.surface: Romeo floundering because he can't live up to expectations in a light romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is not the NATO-alphabet R here; 'finally' takes only his last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to flail about and have great difficulty, so floundering means battling unsuccessfully.

clue.text: Perfect current agreement

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: Describing a present-day contract as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present-day', but it is electric current, written I in formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means exactly as one would wish, without flaw.

clue.text: Sign of damage in rear end of goods vehicle

indicators.note: the rear end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: final letter
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A dent in the back of a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear end' sounds like the back of the lorry, but it picks the last letter of the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on skin or a surface after an injury has healed.

clue.text: Held cold item in chest?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lung is an organ in the chest; the question mark flags the pun on chest as a box

explanation.surface: Keeping something frozen stored in a chest freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' suggests a storage chest or freezer; it is the body's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, meaning gripped tightly, so it matches held.

clue.text: He’s not troubled by first hint of severe spice level

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so its letters are thrown out of order
a first hint is just the opening letter of a word

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
opening letter

explanation.surface: A diner who isn't bothered even by a hint of very hot seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' here simply places the letter after the jumbled part.
explanation.definitionFit: The hotness of a dish is how fiery its chilli or pepper content is, measured on scales like Scoville.

clue.text: Singer looking embarrassed prior to intro

indicators.note: coming prior to something means placed before it in order

blocks.note: an embarrassed face goes red
an intro is the start

explanation.surface: A vocalist blushing just before the song's opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' points to a performer, but in crosswords it often means a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a rusty orange tail, so it qualifies as a warbling creature.

clue.text: Dismal Conservative

blocks.note: first meaning: sad or low in spirits
second meaning: the colour of the Conservative party, in Britain and Canada

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase about a gloomy politician; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word covers both a melancholy mood and the right-of-centre party whose campaign colour it is.
